# Commands

`just` lists every recipe, by group (`just --list`). A recipe that writes says what it writes;
one that writes outside `apply` is a plan unless `confirm=apply` is among its arguments.

<!-- commands: generated by `just docs-readme` from the recipes' [group] and [doc]; edit those -->
**The tool**

| | |
|---|---|
| `just doctor [args ...]` | what this machine has of what the simulated benches need, and what provides a missing one; `--require zephyr,nuttx` makes the exit code say whether those can run |
| `just setup` | the tool's venv, the collections, sops and age (pinned), the git hooks |
| `just pins [args ...]` | the pinned single-file tools on this machine: `list`, `install [name ...]`, `path` (`core/host/binaries.yml`, `docs/GETTING-STARTED.md#requirements`) |
| `just features [args ...]` | the feature index (each collection's `features.yml`): checked against the code by default; `--gaps` what is unproven, `--list` every feature, `--owners <path>...` the features a file belongs to |
| `just test-changed [base=origin/main] [args ...]` | the unit and sim tests a change needs, from what it changed against `base` (default origin/main): the tests of the features it touches and of the files it changed; shared ground (the test harness, plugin loading, requirements, workflows) runs everything |
| `just core-only [args ...]` | the unit tests against core alone: a collections tree with `rxrbench.core` and a fixture plugin, no bundled plugin (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#core-portability` P1) |
| `just privacy` | the privacy check alone: refuse site-private text in the tool's tracked files (`CONTRIBUTING.md#public-and-private`) |
| `just ci [job=containers] [args ...]` | a GitHub Actions job (default `containers`) run here with `act` as GitHub runs it, on a clean clone of HEAD: with the jobs it needs, as a non-root user with sudo; or, for a job with its own image (`mesh-sim`, `sim`), that job alone, as root in its image (needs `act` and Docker) |
| `just docs` | the generated reference into `.build/docs`: the collections' modules, plugins and roles (antsibull-docs, Sphinx) and the Python API (pdoc), from the pinned doc tools |
| `just docs-lint` | antsibull-docs' lint of every collection's docs, as CI runs it |
| `just docs-layout` | write `docs/LAYOUT.md`'s tables and the role specs' layout variables from `docs/layout-vars.yml` (a unit test checks them) |
| `just docs-readme` | write the commands tables (`docs/COMMANDS.md`, each plugin README) from the recipes' `[group]` and `[doc]` (a unit test checks them) |
| `just docs-serve [port=8765]` | serve `.build/docs` on 127.0.0.1, building it first when it is not there |
| `just test` | unit and sim tests (each sim skipped until its images are built), lint, the privacy check; needs no hardware |

**Bench hosts and devices**

| | |
|---|---|
| `just hosts-setup <layout> [args ...]` | a layout's bench hosts up to date: devreg, the registry, the serial brokers (`--check --diff` shows what would change) |
| `just hosts-install <host> [args ...]` | the default install on a bench host or the workstation: tools, venvs, the plug watcher or relay (`-K` when its sudo asks a password) |
| `just enroll <name> <ident> [args ...]` | register a device the survey found, from its facts, and push the registry to the bench hosts; `--layout L --family F (--key V \| --image I)` also declares it in a layout |
| `just cp210x-serial <host> [args ...]` | read or set a CP2102 bridge's serial on a bench host |
| `just devreg [args ...]` | the device registry, from this checkout, against the site's registry: `list`, `scan`, `resolve <name>`, `guard <name> <path>` (`devreg/README.md`) |
| `just survey [host=all] [deep=false] [args ...]` | identify every USB device on a bench host: facts and tags per device (`deep=true` also resets ESP32 boards for chip, flash, PSRAM and eFuse facts); `RXRBENCH_FACTS_COMMIT=1` ends each run with one `chore(facts)` commit |
| `just wsl-attach [names ...]` | on a WSL workstation: attach the registry's workstation boards through usbipd |

**Layouts, read-only**

| | |
|---|---|
| `just inventory <layout>` | the hosts and groups a layout resolves to |
| `just show <layout> <board> [args ...]` | one board's declared state, each value with the file that set it; a dotted key narrows it (`--ansible` also checks the result against ansible-inventory) |
| `just layers <layout>` | the layers a layout inherits, lowest first, and what each brings |
| `just golden <action> [args ...]` | what every layout resolves to, as files: `record` writes it (`--example`: the examples, to `tests/golden/`), `check` diffs the layouts against it; run `check` after a change to the inventory plugin, the layers, the families or the roles |
| `just dump <layout>` | everything Ansible sees for a layout, as YAML (a before/after record for a migration) |
| `just labels <layout>` | a printable sheet of board labels for a layout (name, type, serial tail, host, LED colour) |

**Plan and apply**

| | |
|---|---|
| `just boot <layout> [args ...]` | bootloaders: the plan, or with `confirm=apply` the write; a plan resets nothing, it decides from the bootloader last read (`-e boot_read=true` reads, which resets an ESP32) |
| `just facts <layout> [args ...]` | read every board's actual state; changes nothing |
| `just plan <layout> [args ...]` | what applying a layout would change; changes nothing |
| `just apply <layout> [args ...]` | bring a layout's boards to their declared state: image, radio, config (`--limit <board>`) |
| `just debug <layout> <board> [action=status] [gdb_args ...]` | JTAG on an ESP32-S3 over its console's USB cable: `start`, `attach [gdb args]` (the symbols of exactly the image it runs), `stop`, `status` |
| `just locate <layout> <board> [seconds=60] [args ...]` | blink one board's LED so it can be found (white on a board with a colour); 0 seconds stops it |
| `just reboot <layout> <board> [args ...]` | reboot one board through its console and wait until it answers again (`--check` reads it and sends nothing) |
| `just stage <image> [args ...]` | a catalogued image from its published source (`github` or `url`, sha256-pinned, a zip `member`) into the image store, with the version and build it reports |
| `just diag <layout> [args ...]` | pull diagnostics from every device of a layout into `runs/<time>/<device>/`; changes nothing |
| `just device-test <layout> [args ...]` | run a layout's device tests (`bench_tests`); results in `runs/<time>/<device>/` |
| `just scenario <layout> [args ...]` | run a layout's scenarios (`bench_scenarios`, and the library tests it binds, `bench_test_bindings`): steps across devices, each judged on the board it names, `within` seconds to come true; `runs/<time>/scenario/` |
| `just bench-test <layout> [args ...]` | the whole test of a bench: apply the layout, run its device tests, then its scenarios |
| `just run <layout> [args ...]` | a run of a bench's tests that records its state: the plan writes `runs/<time>/state.json` (what each board was declared and reported, whether the bench was clean), then its device tests and scenarios under the same run |
| `just exercise <layout> <board> [args ...]` | exercise one board of a layout: every verb that applies to it, reads first, then writes each undone within the run, then with `--destructive` the destructive ones each with its restore; `--list` says what applies and why, `--skip <verb,..>` leaves verbs out, `--record` keeps the record as the site's latest for the board and its steps in the site's ledger; `--stale-only` leaves out what passed last time against the same code, board type and firmware (`--max-age DAYS`), `--only <verb,..>` runs those; the record is `runs/<time>/exercise/<board>.json`. It writes to the board: what would run unless `confirm=apply` |
| `just matrix [args ...]` | the capability matrix's table from the site's exercise records (`<site>/exercise/*.json`, the newest per board), written between the markers in `<site>/docs/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md`; `--check` exits 1 when the file is stale, `--stdout` prints the table |
| `just campaign <name> [args ...]` | a campaign (`<site>/campaigns/<name>.yml`): each state (a layout, with overrides) planned, applied, checked clean and tested in turn; a failed apply stops it; `runs/<time>/campaign/<name>/` |
| `just compare [args ...]` | what changed between two runs (`just compare <run> <run>`), or between the states of a campaign run (`just compare <run>`): each device test and scenario, beside what changed on the bench; refuses a run that was not clean unless `--unclean`, and a board read at another identity depth in each run unless `--mixed-depth`; `--json` |
| `just timing [args ...]` | where the time goes: tasks and module phases from the runs' `timing-<play>.json`, slowest first, with how each moved between the oldest and newest run (`--last N`, or run names) |

**Backups and secrets**

| | |
|---|---|
| `just backup <layout> [args ...]` | region backups (the config regions the running image's flash map names) and chip backups of a layout's ESP32, RP2040/RP2350 and probe-wired boards, in `backups/` here (`-e chip=false`: regions only); a board with no backup path is refused unless `-e partial=true` |
| `just restore-regions <layout> <board> [backup=latest] [args ...]` | write a region backup back (the regions where the firmware keeps its config): the board reboots once and comes back as the node it was; a plan unless `confirm=apply` |
| `just snapshot <layout> <name> [args ...]` | a named whole-chip snapshot of a layout's ESP32 and RP2040/RP2350 boards; other boards are refused unless `-e partial=true` |
| `just switch <layout> <name> [args ...]` | put a layout's boards back to a named snapshot; a plan unless `confirm=apply` |
| `just secrets <layout> [args ...]` | what secrets each device holds and whether each is the one it should be (escrowed, or declared); shows none |
| `just keys-export <layout> [args ...]` | escrow the secrets each device made (a node's identity key) into the site's encrypted store; writes nothing to a board (`-e rekey=true` replaces an escrowed key) |
| `just keys-restore <layout> [args ...]` | give each board its escrowed secrets back (an erased or reflashed board becomes the node it was); a plan unless `confirm=apply` |
| `just erase <layout> <board> [region] [args ...]` | erase one named config region of a board (a wedged node's way back); with none named, list them; a plan unless `confirm=apply` |
| `just erase-chip <layout> <board> [args ...]` | erase a board's whole chip, checked to be the registry's; refused without a backup of it (`-e erase_without_backup=true`); a plan unless `confirm=apply` |
| `just restore-chip <layout> <board> [backup=latest] [args ...]` | write a whole-chip backup back, whatever ran on the board since; refused unless the backup was read from this chip; a plan unless `confirm=apply` |
| `just card <layout> <device> <reader> [args ...]` | the checks for writing a device's SD card through a registered reader; `-e card_confirm=<reader>` writes, which erases the card |

**Simulated benches**

| | |
|---|---|
| `just sim-zephyr-build [args ...]` | the Zephyr bench's images for native_sim from any west workspace (`RXRBENCH_ZEPHYR_WORKSPACE`): two shell images (`bare`), two signed SMP server images (`zephyr_mcumgr`) |
| `just sim-qemu-build [args ...]` | the emulated MCU's images (`zq`, `zq-b`): Zephyr's SMP server under MCUboot on Arm's MPS2 AN385, run by `qemu-system-arm` (needs the Zephyr SDK) |
| `just sim-host-setup [args ...]` | the simulated bench host (registry host `vmhost1`): fetch its pinned cloud image and make its keys |
| `just sim-host-up [args ...]` | run the simulated bench host in QEMU, ssh on a loopback port, until stopped |
| `just sim-host-down [args ...]` | stop the simulated bench host |
| `just sim-host-ssh [args ...]` | an ssh session on the simulated bench host |
| `just pcbench-up` | the whole bench on a PC: the simulated host up in the background, with the default install and the simulated boards in it (always against `site.example`) |
| `just pcbench-test [args ...]` | plan, apply, device tests and scenarios of layout `zsim-vm` on the PC bench |
| `just pcbench-down` | stop the PC bench |
| `just sim-zephyr-up [boards ...]` | run the simulated Zephyr bench (layout `zsim`) behind real brokers, until stopped; `zq1` is the emulated MCU |
<!-- commands: end -->

## Recipes a plugin brings

A plugin adds recipes from its own `.just` file, which the justfile imports; its README documents
them:

| Plugin README | Its recipes |
|---|---|
| [`mesh`](../collections/ansible_collections/rxrbench/mesh/README.md) | `sim-up`, `sim-down`, `sim-build`, `sim-build-zephcore` (the simulated mesh bench), `sim-mt-up`, `sim-mt-down`, `sim-mt-pull`, `sim-mt-wipe` (stock Meshtastic in containers), `stage-image`, `net-facts` |
| [`linux`](../collections/ansible_collections/rxrbench/linux/README.md) | `sim-linux-up`, `sim-linux-down`, `sim-linux-reimage` (Linux devices in containers), `sim-vm-up`, `sim-vm-down`, `sim-vm-bundle`, `sim-vm-sandbox` (the A/B machine), `stage-wic` |
| [`zephyr`](../collections/ansible_collections/rxrbench/zephyr/README.md) | `sim-zapp-build` |
| [`nuttx`](../collections/ansible_collections/rxrbench/nuttx/README.md) | `sim-nuttx-build` |
| [`launcher`](../collections/ansible_collections/rxrbench/launcher/README.md) | `launcher` |
